# Reference

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Every public operation of Kairn, grouped by what it does, with the kernel that computes it, and the kernels that the public headers do not call yet. Each kernel has a page: its statement in plain mathematics, the C++ forms that reach it, what it requires, what is proved and with which theorem, its listing, and what the latest brute-force runs measured. [How to read a page](reading.md) explains each part.

The [C++ API](../api/index.md), which Doxygen generates from the comments of the public headers, lists every class, function and macro of `include/kairn/*.hpp` with its declaration and its comment; the comment of an operation names the kernel it calls.

Of the 116 kernels, 109 are proved and 7 are **UNVERIFIED**: [`ball_to_interval_1`](ball_to_interval_1.md), [`interval_mid_rad_1`](interval_mid_rad_1.md), [`interval_mul_2`](interval_mul_2.md), [`interval_split_1`](interval_split_1.md), [`interval_sub_2`](interval_sub_2.md), [`interval_to_ball_1`](interval_to_ball_1.md), [`mul_ext_2_2`](mul_ext_2_2.md).

32 kernels have a statement on finite operands and one on infinite and NaN operands; the second is proved for all of them.

No public operation calls an UNVERIFIED kernel, so none needs the marker `kairn::unverified`.

Notation: $u = 2^{-p}$ is the unit roundoff of the limb type `T` ($2^{-53}$ for `double`, $2^{-24}$ for `float`), $\eta$ its smallest positive number, $\mathrm{RN}$ rounding to nearest with ties to even, and a two-limb number $x = x_0 + x_1$ is *normalized* when $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$ ([Numbers](../developer/design/phase0/numbers.md#notation)). An operand of type `Expansion<T, 1>` next to an `Expansion<T, 2>` is its limb: the form with a limb of type `T` applies.

| `Ball<T, 2>(c, r)`, `Ball<T, 2>(c)`, `Ball<T, 2>(a)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, canonical | [`ball_make_2`](ball_make_2.md) |

## Arithmetic

Sums, differences, products, negation and absolute value. The operators of two limbs return IEEE-like results: canonical infinities and NaN, as `T` does.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a + b`, `a += b`, `add_fast(a, b)`, `a - b`, `a -= b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | $s = \mathrm{RN}(a + b)$; $\lvert s - (a + b)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a + b\rvert$ | [`add_1_1`](add_1_1.md) |
| `a * b`, `a *= b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$; $\lvert p - a b\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a b\rvert + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`mul_1_1`](mul_1_1.md) |
| `x + y`, `x += y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | canonical; the result of [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`add_2_2_full`](add_2_2_full.md) |
| `x + a`, `a + x`, `x += a`, `x + y`, `y + x`, `x += y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | canonical; the result of [`add_2_1`](add_2_1.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`add_2_1_full`](add_2_1_full.md) |
| `x - y`, `x -= y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | canonical; the result of [`sub_2_2`](sub_2_2.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`sub_2_2_full`](sub_2_2_full.md) |
| `x - a`, `x -= a`, `x - y`, `x -= y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | canonical; the result of [`sub_2_1`](sub_2_1.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`sub_2_1_full`](sub_2_1_full.md) |
| `a - y`, `x - y` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | canonical; the result of [`sub_1_2`](sub_1_2.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`sub_1_2_full`](sub_1_2_full.md) |

## Arithmetic without the fix-up

`kairn::finite::`: the finite cores of the operators of two limbs, without the fix-up that makes infinities and NaN canonical; for one limb, the operators themselves.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `finite::add(a, b)`, `finite::sub(a, b)`, `finite::add_fast(a, b)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | $s = \mathrm{RN}(a + b)$; $\lvert s - (a + b)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a + b\rvert$ | [`add_1_1`](add_1_1.md) |
| `finite::mul(a, b)`, `finite::ldexp(a, n)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$; $\lvert p - a b\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a b\rvert + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`mul_1_1`](mul_1_1.md) |
| `finite::add(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (x + y)\rvert \le \frac{3u^2}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert x + y\rvert$, normalized | [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md) |
| `finite::add(x, a)`, `finite::add(a, x)`, `finite::add(x, y)`, `finite::add(y, x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | $\lvert z - (x + a)\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x + a\rvert$, normalized | [`add_2_1`](add_2_1.md) |
| `finite::sub(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (x - y)\rvert \le \frac{3u^2}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert x - y\rvert$, normalized | [`sub_2_2`](sub_2_2.md) |
| `finite::sub(x, a)`, `finite::sub(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | $\lvert z - (x - a)\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x - a\rvert$, normalized | [`sub_2_1`](sub_2_1.md) |
| `finite::sub(a, y)`, `finite::sub(x, y)` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (a - y)\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert a - y\rvert$, normalized | [`sub_1_2`](sub_1_2.md) |
| `finite::mul(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - x y\rvert \le 4\,u^2\,\lvert x y\rvert + \tfrac{3}{2}\,\eta$, normalized | [`mul_2_2`](mul_2_2.md) |
| `finite::mul(x, a)`, `finite::mul(a, x)`, `finite::mul(x, y)`, `finite::mul(y, x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | $\lvert z - x a\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x a\rvert + \eta$, normalized | [`mul_2_1`](mul_2_1.md) |
| `finite::add_fast(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (x + y)\rvert \le 3\,u^2\,(\lvert x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert)$, normalized | [`add_fast_2_2`](add_fast_2_2.md) |
| `finite::ldexp(x, n)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `int` | $\lvert z - x c\rvert \le \eta$, normalized | [`mul_pow2_2`](mul_pow2_2.md) |

| `x == a`, `a == x`, `x != a`, `a != x`, `x == y`, `y == x`, `x != y`, `y != x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | exactly whether $x = a$ | [`eq_2_1`](eq_2_1.md) |
| `a < y`, `y > a`, `x < y`, `y > x` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $a < y$ | [`lt_1_2`](lt_1_2.md) |
| `a <= y`, `y >= a`, `x <= y`, `y >= x` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $a \le y$ | [`le_1_2`](le_1_2.md) |
